aushadhi-open-clinician-rules.changes: Clinician-reviewed internal-evaluation interaction rules deterministically promoted from the attested v2 draft and reviewed mappings.

routes: oral tablet for both exact reviewed product assertions

rules.mechanism: Amiodarone potentiates warfarin's anticoagulant response, increasing PT/INR and the risk of serious or fatal bleeding.
rules.management: Confirm that the prescriber or anticoagulation service has reviewed the warfarin dose and arranged PT/INR monitoring when amiodarone is started, stopped, or changed. Do not independently stop either established medicine or autonomously change the warfarin dose. Use prescriber-directed PT/INR monitoring during coadministration and after amiodarone discontinuation. The interaction can persist for weeks to months after amiodarone discontinuation. Counsel the patient to seek urgent clinical advice for unusual bleeding or bruising, prolonged bleeding, blood in urine, or red or tarry-black stools. The U.S. amiodarone label's numerical warfarin dose-reduction instruction is evidence only and is not an autonomous pharmacy action.

evidence.source: openFDA drug label: amiodarone hydrochloride tablets
evidence.excerpt: The current U.S. label states that amiodarone potentiates warfarin's anticoagulant response, can cause serious or fatal bleeding, requires prothrombin-time monitoring, and can persist for weeks to months after amiodarone discontinuation.

evidence.source: openFDA drug label: warfarin sodium tablets
evidence.excerpt: The current U.S. warfarin label lists amiodarone among relevant CYP inhibitors, requires closer INR monitoring when interacting medicines are started, stopped, or changed, warns of major or fatal bleeding, and identifies reportable bleeding symptoms.

routes: oral tablet for both exact reviewed product assertions

rules.mechanism: Postmarketing reports suggest azithromycin may potentiate oral anticoagulants, although a dedicated azithromycin-warfarin study did not change prothrombin time.
rules.management: Confirm that the prescriber or anticoagulation service has arranged a PT/INR monitoring plan during concomitant oral azithromycin use and will decide whether follow-up is needed when the course ends. Do not independently change a dose or stop either medicine. Use prescriber-directed PT/INR monitoring during concomitant use; no universal schedule or fixed post-discontinuation interval is asserted. Counsel the patient to seek urgent clinical advice for unusual bleeding or bruising, prolonged bleeding, blood in urine, or red or tarry-black stools. This review scope is limited to exact reviewed PMBJP oral-tablet assertions. Oral suspensions, the stale code 48 dispersible-tablet assertion, and every other unreviewed or non-tablet presentation are excluded. The U.S. label describes postmarketing potentiation reports but also states that a dedicated azithromycin-warfarin study did not affect prothrombin time.

evidence.excerpt: Monitor prothrombin time/INR when azithromycin is co-administered with warfarin.

routes: oral tablet for both exact reviewed product assertions

rules.mechanism: Clarithromycin inhibits CYP3A and the US clarithromycin label reports postmarketing potentiation of oral anticoagulant effects, so concomitant use can raise anticoagulant effect and bleeding risk. The magnitude and time course in an individual patient are not established by this source.
rules.management: Confirm that the prescriber or anticoagulation service has arranged a PT/INR monitoring plan during concomitant oral clarithromycin use and will decide whether follow-up is needed when the course ends. Do not independently change a dose or stop either medicine. Use prescriber-directed PT/INR monitoring during concomitant use; no universal schedule or fixed post-discontinuation interval is asserted. Counsel the patient to seek urgent clinical advice for unusual bleeding or bruising, prolonged bleeding, blood in urine, or red or tarry-black stools. This review scope is limited to exact reviewed PMBJP oral-tablet assertions. Erythromycin and every other macrolide are excluded; azithromycin is handled by the separate rule warfarin__azithromycin_oral. The H. pylori combipack (PMBJP code 2097) resolves to a distinct catalogue ingredient identity and is excluded. The 500 mg assertion (PMBJP code 380) is excluded pending official tender evidence and immediate-release disambiguation, because RxNorm exposes both an immediate-release and a 24 HR extended-release 500 mg oral tablet concept. Oral suspensions, injections and every other unreviewed or non-tablet presentation are excluded.

evidence.excerpt: Clarithromycin may potentiate the effects of oral anticoagulants (US clarithromycin label). Supports CLARITHROMYCIN only.

routes: oral tablet for both exact reviewed product assertions

rules.mechanism: Fluconazole inhibits CYP2C9 and CYP3A4 and can increase warfarin anticoagulant effect, PT/INR, and bleeding risk.
rules.management: Confirm that the prescriber or anticoagulation service has reviewed the warfarin dose and arranged PT/INR monitoring when oral fluconazole is started or stopped. Do not independently stop either medicine or autonomously change the warfarin dose. Use prescriber-directed PT/INR monitoring during coadministration and after fluconazole discontinuation. The enzyme-inhibiting effect of fluconazole can persist for 4 to 5 days after discontinuation; the labels do not prescribe a universal PT/INR schedule for that interval. Counsel the patient to seek urgent clinical advice for unusual bleeding or bruising, prolonged bleeding, blood in urine, or red or tarry-black stools. This review scope is limited to exact oral-tablet product assertions. Intravenous fluconazole may be source-relevant but is outside the proposed product scope. The labels do not establish a single-dose exception.

evidence.excerpt: The current U.S. fluconazole label reports increased prothrombin time and bleeding events with warfarin, recommends careful prothrombin-time monitoring, states that warfarin dose adjustment may be necessary, and says fluconazole enzyme inhibition persists 4 to 5 days after discontinuation.

evidence.source: openFDA drug label: warfarin sodium tablets
evidence.excerpt: The current U.S. warfarin label lists fluconazole as a CYP2C9 and CYP3A4 inhibitor, requires closer INR monitoring when interacting medicines and antifungals are started or stopped, warns of major or fatal bleeding, and identifies reportable bleeding symptoms.

routes: oral tablet for both exact reviewed product assertions

rules.mechanism: Oral ketoconazole may enhance warfarin anticoagulant effect; the current warfarin label lists ketoconazole as a CYP3A4 inhibitor with potential to increase warfarin effect.
rules.management: Confirm that the prescriber or anticoagulation service has reviewed the warfarin dose and arranged PT/INR monitoring when oral ketoconazole is started or stopped. Do not independently stop either medicine or autonomously change the warfarin dose. Use prescriber-directed PT/INR monitoring during coadministration and when the interacting medicine is started or stopped. Counsel the patient to seek urgent clinical advice for unusual bleeding or bruising, prolonged bleeding, blood in urine, or red or tarry-black stools. This review scope is limited to the exact oral-tablet product assertion. Ketoconazole soap, lotion, shampoo, cream, and other topical products are excluded.

evidence.excerpt: The current U.S. oral ketoconazole label states that ketoconazole may enhance the anticoagulant effect of coumarin-like drugs and that the effect should be carefully titrated and monitored.

evidence.source: openFDA drug label: warfarin sodium tablets
evidence.excerpt: The current U.S. warfarin label lists Ketoconazole as a CYP inhibitor, requires closer INR monitoring when interacting medicines, antibiotics, or antifungals are started or stopped, and identifies reportable bleeding symptoms.

routes: oral tablet for both exact reviewed product assertions

rules.mechanism: Metronidazole can potentiate warfarin anticoagulant effect and prolong prothrombin time; the current warfarin label also lists metronidazole as a CYP2C9 inhibitor.
rules.management: Confirm that the prescriber or anticoagulation service has reviewed the warfarin dose and arranged PT/INR monitoring when oral metronidazole is started or stopped. Do not independently stop either medicine or autonomously change the warfarin dose. Use prescriber-directed PT/INR monitoring during coadministration and when the interacting medicine is started or stopped. Counsel the patient to seek urgent clinical advice for unusual bleeding or bruising, prolonged bleeding, blood in urine, or red or tarry-black stools. This review scope is limited to exact oral-tablet product assertions. Tinidazole, topical metronidazole, and metronidazole combination suspensions are outside the proposed scope.

evidence.excerpt: The current U.S. metronidazole label reports potentiation of warfarin with prolonged prothrombin time and requires careful PT/INR monitoring. It supports metronidazole only, not tinidazole.

evidence.source: openFDA drug label: warfarin sodium tablets
evidence.excerpt: The current U.S. warfarin label lists Metronidazole as a CYP inhibitor, requires closer INR monitoring when interacting medicines, antibiotics, or antifungals are started or stopped, and identifies reportable bleeding symptoms.

routes: oral tablet for both exact reviewed product assertions

rules.mechanism: Observed clinical, multifactorial: concurrent tramadol is associated with increased INR and serious bleeding on warfarin; tramadol has no intrinsic anticoagulant/antiplatelet pharmacodynamic action, so the mechanism is not a clean single-enzyme PK-perpetrator effect.
rules.management: Confirm that the prescriber or anticoagulation service has reviewed whether the warfarin dose needs adjustment and arranged additional PT/INR monitoring when oral tramadol is started. Use prescriber-directed review when tramadol is stopped. Do not independently change a dose or stop either medicine. Use prescriber-directed PT/INR monitoring when tramadol is started and a prescriber-directed decision about follow-up when it is stopped; no universal schedule or fixed post-discontinuation interval is asserted. Counsel the patient to seek urgent clinical advice for unusual bleeding or bruising, prolonged bleeding, blood in urine, or red or tarry-black stools, and not to stop warfarin without discussing it with a healthcare professional. This review scope is limited to exact reviewed PMBJP oral-tablet assertions. Tramadol injections, combination products, and every other unreviewed or non-tablet presentation are excluded. Major severity is a clinician-approved local mapping for internal evaluation; the retained source is a UK MHRA safety update and does not establish U.S. or Indian regulatory applicability.

evidence.excerpt: MHRA warns of increased INR and major bruising or life-threatening bleeding when warfarin and tramadol are used together.

routes: oral tablet for both exact reviewed product assertions

rules.mechanism: Voriconazole inhibits CYP2C9 and can significantly increase prothrombin time and warfarin anticoagulant effect.
rules.management: Confirm that the prescriber or anticoagulation service has reviewed the warfarin dose and arranged PT/INR monitoring when oral voriconazole is started or stopped. Do not independently stop either medicine or autonomously change the warfarin dose. Use prescriber-directed PT/INR monitoring during coadministration and when the interacting medicine is started or stopped. Counsel the patient to seek urgent clinical advice for unusual bleeding or bruising, prolonged bleeding, blood in urine, or red or tarry-black stools. This review scope is limited to the exact oral-tablet product assertion. Intravenous and other voriconazole presentations are outside the proposed product scope.

evidence.excerpt: The current U.S. voriconazole label reports significantly increased prothrombin time with warfarin through CYP2C9 inhibition and directs close-interval anticoagulation monitoring with clinician-directed dose adjustment.

evidence.source: openFDA drug label: warfarin sodium tablets
evidence.excerpt: The current U.S. warfarin label lists Voriconazole as a CYP inhibitor, requires closer INR monitoring when interacting medicines, antibiotics, or antifungals are started or stopped, and identifies reportable bleeding symptoms.
